title: One unauthenticated request with a malformed Host header and an Upgrade header kills the bot process: the WebSocket upgrade handler parses the Host with new URL() outside any try, and nothing catches the exception

evidence.note: const url = new URL(req.url || '/', `http://${req.headers.host || 'localhost'}`) runs first, before the path and session checks, with no try/catch
server.on('upgrade', handleUpgrade(wss, sessions)): a synchronous throw in an 'upgrade' listener escapes Node's http server as an uncaught exception
no output: there is no process-level handler, so the exception ends the process (same fact as AUD-ANTIRUG-002 / AUD-BUY-005)

evidence.ref: node ws-host-crash.js <snapshot>/src/api/ws/handler.ts <host> (scratch folder outside the repo (Node 22.16.0 by absolute path; no src/ import, no .env, no data/, no live DB; loopback 127.0.0.1 only); the handler.ts:43 line read verbatim from the audit-base snapshot and run in a plain Node http 'upgrade' listener; raw TCP request GET /ws with Upgrade: websocket)
evidence.note: output: Host "127.0.0.1:8080" -> 401, server alive; Host "a b" -> server process EXITED code=1 TypeError: Invalid URL; Host "[" -> EXITED code=1 Invalid URL; Host "x:99999999" -> EXITED code=1 Invalid URL
the recommended remote setup is DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0 behind a TLS proxy; the bot port itself then listens on every interface

sibling_sites_checked: Every Host/URL parse in src/api: server.ts:111-117 and :125-131 (inside try, correct), handler.ts:43 (this finding, no try); every synchronous code in the 'upgrade' path: parseCookies (:18-29, cannot throw on a string), validateSession (map lookup), wss.handleUpgrade (ws answers a bad handshake with 400 itself). Express routes are not affected (express 5 catches handler errors). A browser cannot send a malformed Host (it builds Host from the URL), so this needs a raw client: any local process at the default bind, any host that can reach the port in remote mode. A second, authenticated crash path on the same socket layer (an invalid frame on an open WebSocket) is AUD-API-009.
severity_rationale: S1 STRAND: in the documented remote-access mode any host that can reach the dashboard port can stop the whole bot with one short request and no credentials; the process exit stops every exit monitor, the ExitWorker and anti-rug for all chains until a human restarts it, leaving every open position without an exit. Same impact class as AUD-ANTIRUG-002 (S1). At the default 127.0.0.1 bind only a local process can do it (S2-equivalent there). Not S0: it needs a hostile or broken client, and a restart resumes monitoring. Reproduced on loopback with the exact line from the base snapshot.
recommendation: Parse the upgrade URL inside try/catch (or use url.parse on the path only) and answer 400; wrap the whole upgrade handler so any throw destroys only that socket. Decide the process-level uncaught-exception policy with card OD-6 (AUD-BUY-005). Real-path test: send the malformed request to a running server and assert it stays up. Phase 24 (a pure bug fix, no behaviour decision).
